extracted.intended_audience: general readers; students or researchers of media/television criticism and humor
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography of a prominent television critic (Tom Shales) describing his career, style, influence, and recognition — useful for studying approaches to humorous/caustic media criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withering putdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Shales was known for his withering putdowns of shows he disliked, and was nicknamed "Terrible Tom" and "the Terror of the Tube".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sharp, scathing, memorable insults or putdowns as a stylistic device to signal strong negative judgment; such barbs can become a signature element of a critic's voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blunt, polarizing stance
rubrics_metrics.description: His blunt style could polarize; Forbes wrote: "Forget the middle ground, Shales either loves it or hates it — and his reviews of TV shows and personalities are often unabashed paroxysms of that love or hate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take decisive positions rather than hedging; polarizing, unambiguous judgments can make criticism more forceful and attention-grabbing, though they risk alienating some readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fast-paced, amusing prose (trade-off: depth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forbes: "Like the medium he covers, Shales turns out fast-paced and amusing fare that often lacks depth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor brisk, entertaining pacing and humor to mirror the medium (television). Be aware this approach can trade off analytical depth; writers should balance entertainment value with substantive analysis depending on goals/audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incredibly funny, creative, inventive, and smart writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Described by a peer as setting a standard with writing that was "incredibly funny, creative, inventive and smart."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for originality and intelligence in comedic critique — blend wit with thoughtful insight to elevate humor beyond mere insult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversational, 'barroom discussion' voice
rubrics_metrics.description: His style was described as more akin to a 'barroom discussion with readers than a lecture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a conversational, accessible tone that invites readers in (informal, persona-driven voice) rather than a didactic or academic lecture—this can increase approachability and rapport.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorable barbs for lasting impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Shales called such barbs "a TV critic's only shot at immortality."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crafting memorable lines or barbs can create lasting cultural impact and recognition; use sparingly and cleverly to avoid seeming gratuitous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of major cultural/political events as part of critical significance
rubrics_metrics.description: His Pulitzer Prize for Criticism (1988) included coverage of the Robert Bork Supreme Court nomination hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with consequential cultural or political events in coverage; demonstrating relevance and seriousness through such reporting can contribute to critical recognition and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syndication and visible influence as measures of success
rubrics_metrics.description: His reviews were syndicated in newspapers nationwide, and his influence was such that shows he panned would sometimes include unflattering references to him as inside jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide syndication and being referenced (even negatively) by the subjects of criticism indicate cultural reach and influence; building a distinctive voice and reputation can produce this level of visibility.
